doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Basie's piano and surviving the road with tee shirts
summary: Rossano's influences, Basie's stride playing, Harold Jones's tee shirt tip and how to fold a suit.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He’s amazing. He’s totally amazing. He has the technical prowess to play anything that comes to his mind. But he’s heavily influenced by the older guys: Willie “The Lion,” Basie, Jelly Roll Morton, as players. Fats Waller as a player. You know Basie, everybody thinks of him as just kind of going plink-plink-plink-plink. He was the most feared guy on 52nd Street in his day. He could really play. Listen to “The Kid From Red Bank.” It’s unbelievable. He’s playing stride. He studied with Fats Waller. So he knew how to do it. He just figured out I don’t have to kill myself I’ve got this whole band here. I’ll just fill in the little holes. You know? That became his trademark. So he never broke a sweat again, which is kind of nice. Saves your clothes on the road. That was my dilemma when I was on the road, I was a young guy and had never really been on the road and playing with a big band, sweating profusely every night, to keep clothes fresh. This is a great story. So at one point we’re in California in San Francisco and Harold Jones, the drummer, shows up. He was with I think Natalie Cole at the time and they were on break. So he came to see the band, it was all his old buddies. Because Harold was on the “Live at Birdland” record and the “Standing Ovation” record I think also. Great Basie drummer. He said, “you want to know something?” “What?” He said, “Papa Jo Jones told me ‘wear tee shirts underneath your dress shirt.’” He goes, “the tee shirts, you can buy them anywhere and if they get nasty you just throw them out and buy another one.” He goes, “your dress shirts

— you can get three or four nights out of a dress shirt if you wear a tee shirt.” And he says,” and don’t wear that shirt on the bus to the gig. Only change at the gig.” He goes, “because nobody can smell you from the audience. And it doesn’t matter that the other guys could smell your nasty shirt, you’re getting four days out of a dress shirt.” Survival on the road. And to this day I wear tee shirts. Guys say, “how do you wear those, they’re so constraining.” I say, “because I can get four nights out of a dress shirt. How many nights do you get out of a dress shirt when you don’t wear a tee shirt?” “One.” “Okay. There you go.” So things like that. Warren Vache told me how to fold a suit, that he had learned. I think Benny Golson or somebody taught him that, or maybe Clark. You can fold up a suit inside out and not have any wrinkles. So you didn’t see guys with big suitcases back them, you saw them with a little suitcase. Now of course a lot of guys wore coat and tie when they traveled back then anyway. Bucky still does, and John Pizzarelli. Every picture I see on FaceBook of John Pizzarelli he’s wearing a suit.
Yeah. Joe Wilder and all those guys.
Yeah. They put a suit on every day. But to fold up a suit jacket with no wrinkles in a little carry on bag. Nice.
